title: Seyed M. Marandi: US Strike on Iran Imminent — Gulf States Will Not Survive
summary: Iranian academic Seyed Marandi predicts a renewed US strike on Iran in October 2026 and says Iran would destroy Gulf energy infrastructure, collapsing the Gulf monarchies and the world economy.

assertions.quote: But I believe that we will have war. It could happen before or after the Netanyahu election.
I don't think that if the war restarts we will see a huge regional war between countries.
no more refined goods, no more petrochemicals. And that would immediately lead to global economic catastrophe.

verdicts.note: A Gulf supply shock can push oil far higher and cause recession, but a collapse worse than the 1930s goes well beyond what the 2026 disruption produced.

assertions.quote: I don't think any of the current regimes that are bound to the United States in this region can survive.

verdicts.note: The Gulf monarchies have survived repeated Iranian and Houthi attacks on their infrastructure, and their reserves and security services are large.

assertions.quote: at the end ultimately the relationship with between Iran, Russia, and China is going to become stronger.

verdicts.note: Their cooperation has grown through treaties, trade and arms, but Russia and China gave Iran little military help in its wars.

The three hold an annual trilateral naval exercise and China-based firms sell Iran dual-use parts, but DoD says China's defense relationship with Iran is 'modest' and Beijing is reluctant to deepen it.
DDIS sees Russia deepening ties with China and North Korea, but says cooperation with Iran likely weakened in 2025 because of Iran's war with Israel.
US intelligence expects the four to keep seeking more cooperation, but says divergent interests and fear of confronting the US will limit it, short of a bloc.

at the end of the day, this is this war is about Israel. It's the Israeli regime that's behind the war.

verdicts.note: This Doha-based analysis says the war rested on Israeli-backed calculations and that Netanyahu long pushed for it, finding a receptive partner only in Trump; it shows Israeli influence, not a lobby driving US policy.
